stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta's Llama 3 8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML domains including transformers and text-generation.
The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model deployment practices.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is categorized under key AI/ML tags like 'transformers' and 'llama', signaling relevance in the LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: Apple Screen Sharing Pre-Auth RCE
stories.author: warez.sl0p.foo via fro
bullet_points: A vulnerability has been identified in Apple's Screen Sharing feature.
The flaw is classified as a Pre-Authentication Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability.
This represents a critical security risk requiring immediate attention from Apple users and developers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer community of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster, particularly when utilized with coding agents based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, enhancing privacy.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview state, signaling a push for native Apple ecosystem AI acceleration.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical 'trust and accountability gap' caused by undisclosed system prompts in commercial LLM applications.
Introduces AISPA (Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance), a new user-centric framework for auditing these prompts.
Focuses on systematically examining system prompts to improve transparency and governance in deployed AI systems.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: KAISEN introduces a comprehensive, five-phase audit pipeline specifically designed for subgroup fairness in clinical risk models.
The research addresses a critical gap where existing fairness audit components lack rigorous stress-testing and trust validation.
The pipeline covers the entire lifecycle, including stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Introduces AISPA, a new user-centric framework designed to audit system prompts in LLM applications.
Addresses a critical trust and accountability gap caused by the non-disclosure of system prompts in commercial AI products.
Focuses on systematically examining the instructions that govern the behavior of foundation models.

stories.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
stories.author: Geoff Keeling
bullet_points: The research investigates how aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) to prevent self-attribution of consciousness affects their worldview.
Safety fine-tuning was shown to suppress models' tendency to attribute minds not only to themselves but also to animals and inanimate objects.
The study suggests that this alignment process also drives a measurable reduction in the models' spiritual beliefs.

stories.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
stories.author: Raaz Dwivedi
bullet_points: Introduces ORCA-bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents in a production-fidelity oncall scenario.
Highlights the gap between current LLM capabilities (code generation) and the complex requirements of Root Cause Analysis (RCA).
Tests agents' ability to reason over diverse, noisy production data like metrics, logs, and traces, starting from ambiguous reports.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly re-evaluating its licensing agreement with Google.
The uncertainty is linked to recent concerns over the value proposition of Google's AI Overviews.
The news highlights ongoing tensions between major platforms regarding AI data usage and monetization.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new badge incorporates a removable chip for enhanced security.
The design allows hackers to inspect the badge's internal workings.
The chip's design permits the badge to remain functional even after the conference concludes.

stories.title: Google plans to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is reportedly planning to exempt sanctioned nations from new Android developer verification requirements.
This exemption means developers in countries like Cuba or Iran can continue installing APKs without new restrictions.
The policy change is expected to negatively impact developers operating within these sanctioned regions.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance challenges of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while requiring training on a small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel perception-aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics by integrating realistic, limited onboard sensing (segmentation-masked depth) with comprehensive training-time safety guarantees.
Utilizes adversarial motion priors to regularize and improve the evasive reflexes of the humanoid agent during tasks like dodgeball.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis.
It shifts the focus of retrieval from entire documents to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
This addresses the current limitation where existing search tools only provide ranked lists of papers, forcing manual synthesis.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward to standardize the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current evaluation of CUA trajectories relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as automated judges.
OSReward addresses the fundamental challenge of scaling verification for complex CUA tasks beyond manual human annotation.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: Introduces PAIChecker, a tool designed to identify and check for misalignment between Pull Requests (PRs) and their linked issues.
Highlights a critical flaw in current LLM evaluation benchmarks (like SWE-Bench), where PR-Issue pairings can be inaccurate due to repository complexity.
Addresses the reliability of using PR patches as test oracles when the underlying problem statement (issue description) and solution (PR) are mismatched.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG), specifically its struggle with complex multi-hop reasoning.
Existing methods often rely on independent instance-level matching, failing to capture explicit cross-modal relationships.
The proposed DualG-MRAG decouples macro-reasoning from micro-matching to overcome the graph expansion issue in multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of the same prompt, at equal token cost, can outperform sophisticated planning/critique methods.
The finding implies that increased output length alone might be driving accuracy gains, rather than the inherent value of the advanced reasoning techniques.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance challenges of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while being trained on a relatively small dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a novel, claim-centered infrastructure for synthesizing information from chemistry literature.
It addresses the limitation of traditional search systems that only provide ranked document lists, forcing manual cross-paper assembly.
The system shifts the unit of retrieval from the entire paper to specific, provenance-carrying claims.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
The system leverages repository history, specifically merged pull requests, to create these tasks.
Change2Task ensures tasks are grounded in realistic software states, complete with specifications and verification tools.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a new framework for mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of existing PTQ methods which use uniform bit-widths, ignoring the heterogeneous sensitivity of different transformer components to quantization errors.
The core innovation is using a 'fragility-guided' approach to allocate precision efficiently across various parts of the ViT model.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of a prompt, rather than complex iterative reasoning, can achieve comparable or better accuracy at equal token costs.
This finding implies that the sheer volume of generated text, rather than the sophistication of the prompting strategy, might be a primary driver of performance gains in LLMs.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: The research introduces APO, an Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization method for 3D structure prediction.
It addresses a key limitation of existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO) which require expensive supervised labeling.
This unsupervised approach aims to overcome data scarcity bottlenecks in material science and drug discovery.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis by moving beyond simple document retrieval.
It shifts the focus from retrieving entire papers to retrieving specific, provenance-carrying claims across multiple publications.
This addresses the current bottleneck where scientists must manually assemble scattered findings from numerous sources.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward to standardize the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
CUAs are rapidly advancing, but verifying if they fulfill task instructions at scale is a major challenge.
The field is increasingly relying on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as judges, and this work addresses standardization issues in that process.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Change2Task addresses the need for large, executable datasets to train and evaluate coding AI agents.
The system converts historical merged pull requests from code repositories into structured, verifiable tasks.
It links historical code changes with modern repository states, providing realistic task environments for agent development.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs.
It suggests that for equal token costs, simple repeated sampling of the prompt can outperform sophisticated methods like Reflexion.
The finding implies that the increased text generation inherent in complex methods might be artificially inflating perceived accuracy gains.

stories.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Kaiyan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Frontis-MA1, an AI4AI model designed to pursue recursive self-improvement (RSI) within Machine Learning Engineering.
Presents OpenMLE, an open, full-stack system providing a concrete testbed for RSI research, including environments (OpenMLE-Gym), RL, and evolutionary search.
The research focuses on enabling AI systems to improve the very process of building AI, a key long-term goal in advanced AI development.

stories.title: A 125M model beat a 14B LLM at de-identifying medical text 40 faster, on CPU
stories.author: vadim_albarov
bullet_points: A 125M parameter model outperformed a 14B LLM in medical text de-identification tasks.
The smaller model achieved significantly faster processing (40x faster) while running on a CPU.
The work emphasizes local, on-device processing to ensure data privacy ('Your data never leaves the machine').

stories.title: Context window growth is the silent failure mode in agentic pipelines
stories.author: hannune
bullet_points: Context window growth is identified as a critical, often unmeasured failure mode in agentic pipelines.
These multi-step AI pipelines degrade silently under production load without triggering explicit errors.
The article suggests that insufficient measurement of context window expansion is the primary cause of production instability.
